result: The saturation mutagenesis screen of CDKN2A identified that 17.7% (525 of 2964) of all missense variants were functionally deleterious, 60.2% (1784) were functionally neutral, and 22.1% (655) were of indeterminate function.
evaluation: Both reviewers affirm the quality of the saturation mutagenesis work. The editor states 'This is a saturation mutagenesis screening of CDKN2A gene, successfully assessing the functionality of the missense variants. The work is solid and well-prosecuted.' The anonymous reviewer confirms 'Kimura et al performed a saturation mutagenesis study of CDKN2A to assess functionality of all possible missense variants' and notes the manuscript 'was improved during the revision process.'

result: The functional assay validated benchmark variants with high concordance: 84.4% (27/32) of benchmark pathogenic variants were functionally deleterious, 100% (162/162) of benchmark benign variants were functionally neutral, and 90.3% (28/31) of previously reported functionally deleterious VUSs were confirmed as deleterious.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about the validation of the assay using benchmark variants. The editor describes the work as 'solid and well-prosecuted,' and the anonymous reviewer notes the manuscript 'was improved during the revision process,' implicitly accepting the validation data without critique.

result: All in silico variant effect prediction models showed similar performance when compared to functional classifications, with accuracies ranging from 39.5–85.4%, sensitivities of 0.25–0.98, specificities of 0.27–0.98, positive predictive values of 0.22–0.68, and negative predictive values of 0.87–0.98.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the comparison of in silico models to functional data. The editor states the work is 'solid and well-prosecuted' and will 'serve as a valuable resource for diagnostic labs,' implicitly accepting the in silico comparison findings. The anonymous reviewer does not raise concerns about these specific results.

result: Functionally deleterious variants were enriched within ankyrin repeats 1–3 (21.0–26.3%) and depleted in ankyrin repeat 4 (6.5%) and non-ankyrin repeat regions (6.8%), with specific 10-residue subregions showing enrichment of 37.0–48.0% deleterious variants.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the domain-level analysis of variant distribution. The editor describes the work as 'solid' and the anonymous reviewer confirms the manuscript 'was improved during the revision process,' accepting these structural findings without objection.

result: No residues were identified where all missense variants were functionally deleterious, though five residues (p.G23, p.G55, p.H83, p.D84, p.G89) showed 89.5% (17/19) deleterious variants, while 18 residues were completely tolerant of amino acid substitutions.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the residue-level tolerance findings. The editor affirms the work is 'solid and well-prosecuted,' and the anonymous reviewer does not raise concerns about these specific claims, implicitly accepting the residue-level analysis.

result: Analysis of somatic mutations showed enrichment of functionally deleterious variants (33.5% of 355 unique mutations) compared to all possible variants, with 61.4–67.6% of patients having functionally deleterious mutations, and 32.4–50.0% of deleterious mutations occurring in ankyrin repeat 3.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the somatic mutation analysis. The editor states the work will 'serve as a valuable resource for diagnostic labs as well as cancer geneticists,' implicitly accepting the clinical relevance of the somatic mutation findings. The anonymous reviewer does not raise concerns about these results.

result: The functional assay provides evidence to reclassify 76.2% (301/395) of ClinVar VUSs and 78.8% (208/264) of gnomAD VUSs, with 11.4% (45) ClinVar VUSs and 11.7% (31) gnomAD VUSs classified as functionally deleterious and eligible for reclassification as likely pathogenic.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm the clinical utility of the findings. The editor explicitly states 'this work will serve as a valuable resource for diagnostic labs as well as cancer geneticists,' directly supporting the VUS reclassification potential. The anonymous reviewer does not challenge these claims.

result: Validation experiments showed that codon-optimized CDKN2A and synonymous variants significantly reduced cell proliferation (p<0.0001) while pathogenic variants did not, and CellTag library assays demonstrated stable representation of functionally neutral variants over the assay time course.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about the assay validation experiments. The editor describes the work as 'solid and well-prosecuted,' and the anonymous reviewer notes the manuscript 'was improved during the revision process,' accepting the validation data without critique.

result: Replicate experiments showed high reproducibility with 80.7% (452/560) of variants having identical classifications between replicates, no variants switching between deleterious and neutral classifications, and 98.5% concordance for deleterious variants between gamma GLM and log2 fold change methods.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the reproducibility data. The editor affirms the work is 'solid,' and the anonymous reviewer does not raise concerns about the replicate analysis, implicitly accepting the reproducibility findings.

result: Variants with low representation (<2%) in the cell pool at day 9 showed no statistically significant difference in the proportion classified as functionally deleterious (22.6%) compared to variants with >2% representation (17.0%, p=0.28).
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the analysis of low-representation variants. The editor describes the work as 'solid,' and the anonymous reviewer does not raise concerns about this technical aspect of the assay.

result: Among somatic mutations, 7.3% (26/355) would be classified as pathogenic/likely pathogenic by ACMG guidelines, with p.His83Tyr and p.Asp84Asn being the most prevalent, and colorectal adenocarcinoma showing statistically significant depletion of functionally deleterious mutations (20.4%, adjusted p=5.4×10⁻⁹).
evaluation: Reviewers do not question the ACMG classification analysis or cancer-type specific findings. The editor states the work will serve as 'a valuable resource for diagnostic labs,' supporting the clinical interpretation findings. The anonymous reviewer does not raise concerns.

result: The authors conclude that use of in silico models for clinical variant interpretation may be premature, that their data support current ACMG guidelines treating in silico predictions as supporting evidence only, and that presence of pathogenic variants at a residue should be used with caution for CDKN2A.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these interpretive conclusions. The editor affirms the work is 'solid and well-prosecuted' and will 'serve as a valuable resource,' implicitly accepting the authors' interpretation of clinical implications. The anonymous reviewer does not object to these conclusions.
